entities.evidence: Genesis 9:18 identifies Ham as Canaan’s father. Noah names that son in the curse and says he will serve his brothers.

review.translation: [and he said|0], “[Cursed be|1] [Canaan|2]! [He will be|5] [a slave of|3] [slaves|4] [to his brothers|6].”

analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Broaden the proposed Qal definition to include a curse pronounced on a thing, and cite the feminine participle applied to the ground.
draft.definition: To pronounce a curse on someone or something. The passive participle describes whoever or whatever is under the curse.
draft.evidence: In Gen.3.17 Yahweh addresses Adam, but the subject of אֲרוּרָה is הָאֲדָמָה, the ground. In Gen.3.14 the corresponding masculine form אָרוּר describes the serpent.

analysis.evidence: Noah pronounces the curse with אָרוּר כְּנָעַן, “Cursed be Canaan.” The following clause specifies its consequence: Canaan will be a slave to his brothers.
analysis.morphology: Qal passive participle, masculine singular absolute, agreeing with כְּנָעַן.
analysis.sense: To pronounce a curse on someone or something.

analysis.evidence: אָרוּר כְּנָעַן means “Cursed is Canaan.” The prediction that he will be a servant לְאֶחָיו, “to his brothers,” identifies Canaan as a family member.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun in its pausal form, without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עֶבֶד עֲבָדִים means “a slave of slaves.” The repetition intensifies the curse, placing Canaan in the lowest position of servitude to his brothers.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, followed by the plural עֲבָדִים.

analysis.evidence: Noah says that Canaan will be עֶבֶד עֲבָדִים, literally ‘a slave of slaves,’ to his brothers. The plural עֲבָדִים intensifies the singular עֶבֶד, describing Canaan as the lowliest slave.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural, in the absolute state. It completes the construct phrase עֶבֶד עֲבָדִים.

analysis.evidence: The curse places עֶבֶד עֲבָדִים (“a slave of slaves”) before יִהְיֶה as its predicate. The verb states what Canaan shall be, and לְאֶחָיו identifies whom he shall serve.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular, with Canaan as its subject.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: Noah names Canaan and says he will be עֶבֶד עֲבָדִים, a servant of servants. לְאֶחָיו identifies whom Canaan will serve, his brothers.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ precedes the masculine plural construct of אָח. The third-person masculine singular suffix refers to Canaan.
